os_version: Windows 11 Pro 26100, live in-use machine; Microsoft 365 Word 16.0 installed by the user mid-campaign (one UAC click — the human-in-the-loop step recorded in windows-office-object-model)
app: Microsoft Word 16.0 via COM automation — the brief's Tier C star case: the document itself, above any render tree. Throwaway document, closed without saving

stack_detection.signature: Dispatch('Word.Application') answers in 10 ms (REGDB check is a registry read — free and a-priori)

channel_setup: pywin32 Dispatch('Word.Application'), Visible=True for the dual-channel and pixel ground truth. No flags, no permissions beyond having Office.

t1_read_text.detail: Sentinel written through Range().InsertAfter in 14.5 ms, read back through Range().Text in 4.6 ms, char-exact including accents and CJK ('café naïve élève 日本語'). The document as a structured source: 79 bytes / 18 tokens for content whose window screenshot costs 1446 tokens — 80x, the strongest single ratio in the study (Linux UNO was ~65x).

t2_enumerate.detail: The object model enumerates DOCUMENT structure (paragraphs, ranges, shapes), not UI; UI enumeration belongs to the UIA dual (Word's ribbon/window distills to 1605 tokens).

t3_live_value.detail: Both directions live: (a) keyboard-typed text (' TYPED-9k4x', foreground-verified) immediately visible in Range().Text — the model tracks the user's edits; (b) COM-written text immediately present in the UIA channel via TextPattern (see cross-channel note).

t4_living_screen.detail: Idle: two Range().Text reads 1 s apart byte-identical. No self-updating content in a static document.

t5_blind_action.detail: Not needed at this level — the object model ACTS semantically (InsertAfter, AddPicture) with no coordinates at all; the pixel-space question does not arise. Aiming belongs to the paired UIA channel.

t6_pictorial.detail: Inserted a PNG via InlineShapes.AddPicture: the pictorial content is a FIRST-CLASS OBJECT — InlineShapes.Count=1, Type=3 (wdInlineShapePicture), dimensions 12x12 pt. Above the render tree, opaque regions are not merely declared rects, they are addressable objects.

measurements.notes: The star case delivers as predicted: 18 tok vs 1446 (80x), 4.6 ms reads, 14.5 ms writes, char-exact unicode, live in both directions, pictorial content addressable. Family complete across OSes: UNO 21 tok (Linux), Pages/AppleScript 21 tok (macOS), Shell COM 28 tok + Word 18 tok (Windows). METHOD NOTE kept for honesty: the first cross-channel check reported the COM-written text ABSENT from UIA — that was our distiller only querying ValuePattern; a direct TextPattern read on Word's DocumentControl returns the document text exactly ('UIA-CHECK-SENTINEL abc 123'). Not a channel divergence — an extractor gap, the same lesson as macOS ('the router under-used the view'): Word exposes the document to BOTH channels correctly.

runtime_verification.method: cross-channel (COM write -> UIA TextPattern read; keyboard type -> COM read) + PrintWindow capture of the Word window
runtime_verification.agreement: full agreement once TextPattern is used; pixels consistent

permissions_required: Microsoft Office installed (user performed the UAC-gated install)
